summary.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 71% YoY to about INR108 crore, with Hobel Bellows consolidated for two months and a 36.5% EBITDA margin.
summary.overview: Revenue for Q1 FY27 was about INR108 crore, up 71% YoY and 32% QoQ, with Hobel Bellows contributing about INR22 crore over two months. PAT was about INR28 crore (24% margin), up 46% YoY, though other income of INR7 crore (vs INR15 crore in Q4 FY26) flatters the quarter less than in the prior quarter. Management guided Q2 to be stronger, with three months of Hobel and a heavier precision component (PCA) contribution in H2. Confirmed order book stood at about INR280 crore including Hobel, slightly lower QoQ, which management attributed to customer pull-ins; the company also signed a USD7.5 million five-year supply agreement with FACC Austria.

segments.name: Aero tooling
segments.commentary: Contributed approx. 76% of Q1 revenue; management said demand visibility is constructive for next quarter and is dominated by aero engine tooling. Tooling orders are largely PO-to-PO.

segments.name: Precision component and assembly (PCA)
segments.commentary: Covers nuclear, semiconductor, aerospace and Hobel Bellows, making up the remaining 24% of revenue. Management expects a much heavier PCA-led contribution in H2 FY27; about 80% of qualified PCA parts are moving into serial production.

segments.name: Hobel Bellows
segments.commentary: Contributed 21% of Q1 revenue (about INR22 crore for two months). Management guides 15-20% growth for this business; AS9100 certification for Vizag facility targeted by Q4 FY27.

segments.name: Nuclear
segments.commentary: Cumulative nuclear order wins of approx. INR87 crore, with about 50% of the existing order book to execute in FY27, mainly in H2.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27 expected to be stronger, with higher revenue and robust EBITDA margins, supported by three months of Hobel consolidation.
Blended gross margin of 65% seen as sustainable for FY27.
Consolidated EBITDA margin of about 34-35% expected for FY27, versus a long-run 30-32%+ range.
Other income expected to be roughly half of Q1 level in Q2 onwards.
Working capital days expected to rise gradually to 160+ days by end of FY27.
Gross block by end-FY27 expected to be about double the current level, mainly due to Saudi JV capex.
ROCE of about 15-16% expected to hold for calendar 2026, rising to 20-21%+ with higher utilisation; asset turns of about 2.5x over 2-3 years.
Two new customers (locomotive and power generation) expected to be onboarded by end FY27, subject to qualification.
capex_capacity: Manufacturing facilities at approx. 58% utilisation; about 10% of available capacity committed to new product introduction and qualification programs.
Capacity expansion being advanced earlier than originally planned to serve qualification programs converting into serial production; no significant core business capex was planned for FY27 earlier.
Saudi JV (Dheya/Kanoo venture) capex to proceed as scheduled; approx. USD10 million infusion into the JV expected in August 2026.
Board approved a QIP enabling resolution of up to INR750 crore; management said this is not an immediate fundraise.
Dheya Engineering seeking about USD10 million via equity and debt; Unimech intends to participate, with possible modest dilution.
demand_pricing: FACC Austria long-term supply agreement: initial value USD7.5 million over five years, with scope for expansion; marks entry into recurring aerospace component supply.
Discussions with one leading engine Tier-1 at an advanced stage; qualification and commercial talks ongoing with several airframe and engine Tier-1s.

Confirmed order book about INR280 crore including Hobel as of 30 June 2026; tooling backlog mostly consumed within the quarter, precision parts over about six months, nuclear INR87 crore split across H2 FY27 and FY28.
165 FAIs completed in the quarter; six new prospective customers engaged.
Four new nuclear reactors in the pipeline; management eyeing these opportunities.
Tariff risk: free trade warehousing zone is fully operational; management says it is watchful, with new European and Saudi exposure as hedges.

qa_highlights.question: Order execution timeline, current order pipeline and nuclear order book outlook (INR87 crore)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the INR280 crore order book is confirmed POs only, excluding FACC forecasts. Tooling backlog mostly gets consumed within the quarter, precision parts over about six months, and nuclear INR87 crore runs into H2 FY27 with some portion in FY28. New nuclear bits are in the pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: Expected revenue growth and gross/EBITDA margin range for FY27, and capex needs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guides one quarter at a time: Q2 to be stronger with three months of Hobel, and H2 to see a much heavier PCA-led contribution. Blended gross margin of 65% is seen as sustainable for FY27. The company is open to further investment and will plan capacity early.

qa_highlights.question: Tooling mix between engine and airframe, and growth from SKU expansion versus existing programmes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a precise mix but said it is dominated by aero engine components, with airframe tooling an opportunity being explored. Growth will come from both SKU expansion and underlying end-consumer demand.

qa_highlights.question: Where Unimech sits in the value chain across precision components and aerospace?
qa_highlights.answer: In semiconductors and PCA it is already Tier-1 and deals directly with OEMs. In aerospace it is largely Tier-2, with some direct OEM work. In nuclear it is mostly Tier-2 where EPC contractors are involved.

qa_highlights.question: Nuclear margins and the nuclear mix two years out?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not disclose segment margins. Consolidated EBITDA margin is guided at 30-32%+ long run and about 34-35% for FY27. Four new nuclear reactors are being pursued.

qa_highlights.question: Hobel Bellows revenue and margin, and expected growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Hobel contributed about INR22 crore over two months. Segment margin is not disclosed; consolidated EBITDA was 36.5%. Growth is guided at 15-20%, though management called it premature to treat as a trend.

qa_highlights.question: Will other income normalise, and what is the FY27 trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 other income fell to INR7 crore because investable funds were deployed into the Hobel acquisition. Q2 onwards other income should be about half the Q1 level. FY26 other income was about INR46 crore.

qa_highlights.question: FACC agreement scope over two to three years, and ROCE and asset turn outlook as utilisation rises?
qa_highlights.answer: The FACC deal is a wave-specific agreement, and scope grows as new RFQs arrive. Asset turns are about 2x currently, expected at 2.5x over two to three years. ROCE of 15-16% holds for calendar 2026, rising to 20-21%+ with higher utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of potential US tariffs and the QIP plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the impact is hard to quantify. Mitigants include the free trade warehousing zone, European customers and the Saudi JV. The INR750 crore QIP is an enabling resolution to meet the minimum public shareholding requirement within 18 months, not an immediate raise. M&A is open for both organic and inorganic growth.

risks_watch: Order book slipped marginally QoQ to about INR280 crore; management attributes this to customer pull-ins, so Q2 order inflow and book replenishment need tracking.
Working capital days guided up from about 130 to 160+ by end FY27 as long-cycle aerospace and nuclear programmes build inventory, which pressures ROCE and cash flow.

Gross block to roughly double by end FY27 mainly on Saudi JV capex, with about USD10 million infusion into the JV in August 2026 and an earlier-than-planned capacity expansion; watch return on this capital.
Other income falling to about half of Q1 INR7 crore from Q2 means earnings depend more on operations; the 36.5% Q1 EBITDA margin needs to hold against the 34-35% FY27 guide.

Nuclear INR87 crore order book is mostly H2 FY27 and the rest FY28; the Hobel AS9100 certification by Q4 FY27 is needed for aerospace entry; the Dheya USD10 million fundraise may cause modest dilution.

Potential US tariffs (100% on India was raised by an investor) remain unquantified by management; the QIP of up to INR750 crore is an enabling resolution, so the timing of any raise is an open question.

Our consolidated order book, including Hobel Bellows, stood at approximately INR280 crores as of 30th June, marginally lower than the level indicated with the previously consolidated order book, including Hobel.
So, close to around 34%-35% of margins is what we will be able to deliver for this financial year.
So, this INR280 crores is the confirmed order book.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, margins and the FY27 growth trajectory, but cautious and deliberately vague on specifics. Management declined to disclose segment margins, the tooling engine/airframe mix, the Leap engine customer and the tariff impact, and it guides only one quarter at a time.
